title: Timeouts kill Docker clients while container workloads continue
reasoning: Killing the local docker run or docker exec client does not terminate the daemon-managed workload. One-shot execution never records a container identity for removal, and --rm only removes a container after it exits. Streaming timeouts leave the command running inside the persistent container until a later container cleanup. Timed-out workloads can continue consuming resources and modifying mounted files after a timeout result is returned.
reproduction: Run a command that waits beyond its timeout and then writes a workspace marker. Keep the streaming runtime alive, or call one-shot cleanup, and observe that the marker can still be written.
recommendation: Track and explicitly terminate the daemon-side execution on timeout and cancellation. For one-shot runs, retain a unique container identity and force removal; for streaming runs, terminate the command process group or stop and recreate the container.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Timeout tests only assert timed_out. Streaming tests immediately clean up the container and neither suite checks that workload side effects stop.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend timeout and cancellation scenarios to assert that delayed writes never occur and no timed-out workload remains running.
minimumFixScope: Timeout and cancellation lifecycle in both runtimes.

history.reasoning: Both evidence files and original line ranges still exist, but the lifecycle changed. exec.py:268-270 now records a unique container name; timeout, finally, and kill paths force-remove it (311, 323, 383). streaming.py:460-470 now calls kill on cancellation and timeout, removing the persistent container at 518. These changes address the original client-only termination mechanism. However, removal failures are suppressed and container identities cleared without confirming termination. Existing timeout tests still only assert timed_out and immediately clean up; they do not verify delayed writes or cancellation. No linked patch attempts or validation results were supplied. Live workload validation was not performed under the read-only restrictions, so a verified fix cannot be concluded.
